# Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis

**Authors:** Zoe Rocke, Mariya Belyayeva

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis (SSPE) is a rare complication due to persistent measles infection. This neurological sequela typically presents in early adolescence and has a progressive course with a high mortality rate. Vaccination implementation has been effective in reducing the number of Measles cases, thereby reducing cases of SSPE. However, measles remains endemic in many countries with poor access to vaccinations. Also, there has been a re-emergence of measles in industrialized countries due to vaccination refusal.
